title: Harden iMessage send: SMS-service fallback + group-chat targeting in the AppleScript path
scope:
JARVIS already SENDS iMessages: the send_message tool (packages/jarvis-core/src/tools/send-message.ts) supports app:'imessage', and apps/desktop/src/actions/confirm-gate.ts routes it through buildIMessageSend + runAppleScript (apps/desktop/src/actions/applescript.ts). The current script (applescript.ts ~:42-52) resolves `participant "<recipient>" of (1st service whose service type = iMessage)`, which works for existing iMessage conversations but has two gaps the scout flagged: (a) NO SMS fallback — a green-bubble / iMessage-unreachable contact silently fails; (b) NO group-chat support — it only targets a single participant.

DO (keep it small + safe, do NOT regress the working iMessage path):
1. In applescript.ts buildIMessageSend: if the iMessage participant send fails/isn't reachable, fall back to sending via the SMS service (`1st service whose service type = SMS`) when available, so US SMS contacts still get the message. Structure it as a try iMessage then fall back, within the AppleScript (or by detecting reachability). Keep behavior identical for normal iMessage contacts.
2. Add group-chat targeting: if the recipient looks like a chat/group identifier (or an explicit group flag), target `chat id "<...>"` / `text chat` instead of a single participant. If detecting groups is unreliable, at minimum do not break single-recipient sends and leave a clear TODO — do not half-break the common path.
3. Do not change the send_message tool schema or the confirm-gate flow.

This is a desktop-only, small hardening. Commit atomically. Verify: desktop typecheck green (pnpm --filter desktop typecheck). AppleScript can't be unit-tested here, so keep the change minimal and clearly correct; a healthy single-recipient iMessage send must still work.
criteria: buildIMessageSend attempts iMessage first and falls back to the SMS service for contacts not reachable via iMessage, so US SMS recipients still receive the message.
Group/chat targeting is supported (target a chat id) OR, if unreliable to detect, single-recipient sends are provably unaffected and a clear TODO is left — never a half-broken common path.
No change to the send_message tool schema or the confirm-gate spoken-confirmation flow; normal single iMessage sends behave exactly as before.
